newsitem.title: USA: Plymouth, Conn., mulls $25.6 mln finance plan.
newsitem.headline: Plymouth, Conn., mulls $25.6 mln finance plan.

text.p: The $25.6 million budget being proposed by the board of finance for the 1997-1998 fiscal year received favorable reviews Tuesday from the town council and members of the Plymouth Taxpayers Association, the Hartford Courant reported Thursday.
A proposed bond issue for the Fisher Middle School was not included in the budget, but will be put on a referendum later in the spring, the Courant reported.
The budget is almost identical to the current year budget and would not require a tax increase. The tax rate is 31.8 mills.
The board of finance approved its proposed budget last week, and the council on Tuesday scheduled the annual budget neeting for May 12.
The board of education saw its requested operating budget cut from $15.4 million to $14.9 million, which means its budget would be the same as this year's.

The school board requested $588,000 to pay for a new roof at Fisher Middle School and a new air-quality system there. The finance board decided not to include that in the town budget but borrow money for the project by issuing bonds. That will require a referendum in the late spring.
